text:
Maria: quick sync — decision council asked us to pick sequencing for two epics: 1) API-first per-request controls (routing, cost hints, per-call QoS) and 2) Console-first rollout workflows (templates, canary UI, traffic splits). Need a prioritization framework discussion.
Sam: +1, we keep getting customer asks for per-request control (low friction for engineers). But it's not trivial.
Jia: devex perspective — API features reduce friction for backend engineers but Console UX unlocks product managers and non-engineer admins. Different personas.
Oliver: sales — biggest enterprise deals repeatedly ask for console rollouts (audit, canary, policy templates). Win or lose revenue there.
Ana: research — we have telemetry showing ~30% of hosted traffic is from small PLG apps; API improvements help that cohort. Enterprise traffic is heavy hitters that care about console workflows.
Sam: propose RICE-style quick calc on both epics in-thread so we can surface a recommendation. Keep it lean: Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort as 1-10.
Maria: yep. I'll start with API-first epic:
Maria: Reach: 7 (PLG + mid-market developers), Impact: 7 (reduces dev friction, faster time-to-value), Confidence: 6 (we've done some proto work), Effort: 6 (several runtime + API surface changes).
Sam: Console-first epic:
Sam: Reach: 5 (mostly enterprise admins + platform teams), Impact: 8 (higher contract value, reduces churn), Confidence: 6, Effort: 8 (UI, backend orchestration, RBAC, audit).
Jia: quick math with RICE score = (Reach*Impact*Confidence)/Effort:
Jia: API-first = (7*7*6)/6 = 49
Jia: Console-first = (5*8*6)/8 = 30
Oliver: raw RICE favors API-first, but that hides strategic enterprise motions. If we close a single enterprise deal with console, ARR impact > dozens of PLG customers. RICE is good for product-led prioritization but misses deal-based multipliers.
Ana: agree. We should add a "deal multiplier" or include expected ARPA in Impact. For Console, Impact should factor dollars and churn reduction, not just user count.
Maria: good point. Let's add a secondary view: revenue-weighted impact. Rough numbers: API-first expected net new ARR per quarter ~50k (many small users); Console-first expected ARR per quarter from a few enterprise deals ~300k if we land two deals.
Sam: then revenue-weighted Impact for console becomes much higher. But effort is also higher and cross-team coordination cost is real.
Jia: we also need launch criteria: minimal viable API controls (request-level cost hint + routing key + toggle header) vs minimal console release (create template, run canary against percentage, audit log). Which one has safer rollout surface area?
Sam: API changes are lower blast radius if we gate them behind flags; runtime already supports routing keys mostly. Console requires orchestration that touches live traffic and needs strong SLOs.
Maria: so risk-wise API < Console. But customer urgency for Console + sales influence high.
Oliver: add sequence option C: do a thin API-first bet that unlocks most enterprise asks (expose policy hooks via API) and follow with Console templates that consume those hooks. That reduces duplicated effort.
Ana: that seems promising. Deliver primitives first (API) and build UX around them. It also helps PLG and removes engineering blockers for enterprise proof-of-concept.
Sam: timeline sketch: primitives (API) = 6 weeks (proto + docs + client examples); console templates = 10-12 weeks after primitives. Parallelize some UI work. But console full feature set is 3-4 months.
Jia: constraints: we have a Q2 frontend sprint heavy on billing work. Console work would compete for devex/design capacity.
Maria: prioritization framework proposal: 1) Run RICE but supplement with two modifiers: revenue multiplier and risk multiplier. 2) Sequence by building shared primitives (API) first when they reduce future effort for console. 3) Define clear launch criteria for each milestone and a canary plan.
Sam: launch criteria proposals: API primitives milestone: a) API spec doc + OpenAPI, b) integration test with runtime, c) sample integration + docs, d) gated flag + canary in region. Console MVP milestone: a) template create/apply UI, b) traffic split enforcement via execution engine, c) audit logs + RBAC, d) customer beta for 1 partner.
Oliver: also insist on sales enablement checklist before GA for Console: playbook, demo tenant, and two committed pilots.
Ana: risk: if we ship API primitives without console, enterprise customers may prototype but stall without productized templates. So we should commit to the console timeline publicly with sales.
Maria: negotiation tactic: we tell sales we'll prioritize API primitives in next sprint and commit to a console beta in 10-12 weeks. That gives sales something to promise and keeps eng scope limited.
Jia: ops note: we should add observability signals to each milestone: per-route latency, rollout failure rate, and config drift alerts.
Sam: technical tradeoffs to watch: per-request controls increase header parsing and routing checks; need to measure p95 overhead. If overhead > 2ms we may need kernel optimizations.
Maria: action items: a) Sam to draft RICE + revenue and risk modifiers and a one-pager by EOD Tue. b) Jia to list devex/design constraints and suggested MVP console flows. c) Oliver to surface two target enterprise customers willing to pilot. d) Ana to validate ARR estimates with finance. e) Maria to schedule decision council review next Friday.
Oliver: +1, will ping enterprise reps.
Sam: noted. I'll include an example API spec snippet in the one-pager:
Sam: ```
POST /v1/infer
Headers: X-Redwood-Route: low-cost
Body: {"model":"mix-medium","prompt":"..."}
Response: streaming tokens
```
Sam: and an example header for rollout: `X-Redwood-Policy: beta-rollout-42`
Jia: can we add a console mock screenshot in the doc? I have a simple Figma frame.
Maria: yes attach it to the one-pager.
deploy-bot: scheduled meeting created: Decision Council — API vs Console sequencing review — Fri 10:00am. Organizer: maria.pm
Maria: thanks. If anyone has a hard objection to the primitives-first sequencing, speak now or bring proximate evidence to Friday's review.
Oliver: no hard objections, just want commitments.
Ana: leaning in favor of primitives-first with strict timeline for console.
Jia: same.
Sam: same.
Maria: closing for now. We'll collate RICE calc + revenue modifiers in the doc.
